newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on export competition.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on export competition.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower as persistent reminders of stiff competition from overseas customers weighing on prices, traders said.
Nearby September led the way down on long liqudiation before expiration of that contract slated for 1201 CDT. The September went off the board at $4.22 per bushel, down 10-1/2 cents per bushel.

The wheat market continues to get hit by increasing supplies of wheat in other countries, steep price levels in the United States compared with others and the recent decision by the EU to reinstate subsidies on export sales, they said.
"With the rebate in Europe this morning it just showed you the trend of the market is down. They're giving it away again," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

Grain traders said early Thursday in Paris the EU granted licenses to export 237,470 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a maximum refund of 4.97 Ecus per tonne. The EU also granted refunds for the export of some barley and wheat flour.
Cargill Inc sold 3.5 million bushels of December and LIT America sold 3.5 million December, the traders said.
Wheat closed four to 10-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 7-1/2 at $4.16-3/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, up from 17,467 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 500 December $4.80 calls at three cents and FIMAT Futures bought 200 December $4.80 calls at 2-1/2 cents, the traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, down from 5,323 Wednesday.
